title: Create an event via right-click 'New Event' on a grid cell
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit (event creation requires Edit; spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Right-click a technician's cell on a working day.
2. Choose 'New Event' from the context menu.
3. Fill in a name (for example 'ZZAUTOTEST stand-up'), keep the date/times offered, and save.
expected: 1. The right-click context menu contains 'New Event'.
2. The event modal opens with the clicked cell's technician and date pre-set.
3. Saving creates an event block on that technician's day.
4. A toast with Undo appears.
notes: 'New Event' is the spec's wording - confirm the exact menu label live. Pre-fill behavior is derived (anchored creation) - confirm live.

title: Create an event by clicking empty grid space in day view, with a live preview block and drag-to-resize
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page in DAY view.
steps: 1. Click (or click-drag) an empty spot on a technician's timeline.
2. While creating, watch the block and try dragging to size it.
3. Complete the event creation.
expected: 1. Clicking empty day-view space starts event creation at that time.
2. A live preview block is shown while creating, and dragging resizes it.
3. Completing creates the event at the previewed time/duration.
notes: Exact create gesture (single click vs click-drag) unpinned - capture live.

title: Event modal offers name, date, start/end time, an all-day toggle, and a color category
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the event modal open (via right-click 'New Event').
steps: 1. Read the fields the modal offers.
2. Fill each: name, date, start and end time, and pick a color category.
3. Save.
expected: 1. The modal contains: name, date, start/end time, an all-day toggle, and a color category.
2. The event saves with the entered values.
3. Re-opening the event shows the saved values.
notes: Field labels unpinned - confirm the exact on-screen labels live.

title: The all-day toggle creates an all-day event
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. You are on the Schedule page with the event modal open.
steps: 1. Turn the all-day toggle ON.
2. Save the event.
3. Look at how it renders in day and week views.
expected: 1. With all-day on, specific start/end times are not required (the time fields are disabled or hidden).
2. The event is created as an all-day block for that technician and day.
notes: All-day rendering (where the block sits on the timeline) unpinned - capture live.

title: Events can be dragged to another technician or another day
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. An event exists on a technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Drag the event block to a different technician's row.
2. Drag it to a different day.
3. Undo/move back to restore.
expected: 1. Dropping on another technician reassigns the event to them.
2. Dropping on another day moves it to that day.
3. Each move produces a toast with Undo.

title: Event cards are structurally distinct from shift cards - white outlined card with a grey icon chip, no colored left rail
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. An event and a shift sit near each other on the grid.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Compare the event card with the shift block side by side.
expected: 1. The event card is a white/neutral card with a thin, even border on all four sides and NO colored left rail (the left rail is the shift's cue).
2. It has a small grey-filled rounded chip on the left containing a calendar icon, and two lines of text beside it: the event name, then the time range in secondary text.
3. The shift reads as a tinted color-filled block with a colored left rail - the two types are separable at a glance, not by color alone.
notes: Visual anatomy is spec-prose only (no designs) - confirm every visual detail live.

title: Events default to neutral/grey; choosing a color tints the card and its icon chip
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to change color; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A newly created event exists with no color chosen.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Look at the new event's default color.
2. Open the event and choose a color from the color picker.
3. Look at the card again.
expected: 1. The default event color is neutral/grey.
2. The color picker offers the same custom color palette as shifts (shared picker with editable labels).
3. Choosing a color tints the card and the icon chip in matching tones, the same way a colored shift is tinted.

title: Double-booked: two work orders overlapping on the same technician at the same time are flagged
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Two different work orders have schedulable lines.
3. You are on the Schedule page; note the toolbar conflict pill's current count.
steps: 1. Schedule work order 1 on a technician for a given time.
2. Schedule work order 2 on the SAME technician overlapping the same time.
3. Look at the two blocks and the toolbar conflict pill.
expected: 1. The overlap is detected as a Double-booked conflict.
2. A warning icon appears on the affected block(s).
3. The toolbar conflict pill's count increases.
4. The conflict is listed in the pill's dropdown.
notes: Conflict-type display names ('Double-booked' etc.) are the spec's words - confirm on-screen wording live. Whether one or both blocks get the icon is unpinned - observe.

title: Weekend shift: a shift on Saturday or Sunday is flagged as a conflict
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Saturday/Sunday columns are visible (View Options - Saturday and Sunday on).
3. A schedulable work order line exists.
steps: 1. Drop the line onto a technician's SATURDAY cell.
2. Look at the block and the conflict pill.
expected: 1. The shift is created but flagged as a Weekend shift conflict (outside working days).
2. The warning icon appears on the block and the conflict is listed in the toolbar dropdown.

title: Before hours: a shift starting before the working-day start is flagged
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician has a known working-day start (for example 8:00 AM).
3. A shift exists for that technician.
steps: 1. In day view, drag the shift so it starts BEFORE the technician's working-day start (for example 6:00 AM).
2. Look at the block and the conflict pill.
expected: 1. The shift is flagged as a Before hours conflict.
2. Warning icon on the block; the conflict appears in the toolbar dropdown.

title: After hours: a shift extending past the working-day end is flagged
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. A technician has a known working-day end (for example 5:00 PM).
3. A shift exists for that technician ending before 5:00 PM.
steps: 1. In day view, drag the shift's right edge so it extends PAST the working-day end (for example to 7:00 PM).
2. Look at the block and the conflict pill.
expected: 1. The shift is flagged as an After hours conflict.
2. Warning icon on the block; the conflict appears in the toolbar dropdown.

title: The toolbar conflict pill shows the issue count and opens a dropdown listing the conflicts
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. At least two conflicts of different types exist (for example one double-booked overlap and one Saturday shift - create them first).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Read the conflict pill in the grid toolbar.
2. Click it.
3. Read the dropdown.
expected: 1. The pill shows the current number of scheduling issues.
2. Clicking opens a dropdown listing each conflict.
3. The list covers all current conflicts (count matches the pill).
4. Resolving a conflict (for example moving the shift) reduces the count - detection is continuous.

title: Clicking a conflict in the dropdown navigates to the relevant technician and day
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A conflict exists on a technician/day that is NOT currently in view (navigate the grid away first).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Open the conflict pill's dropdown.
2. Click the conflict entry.
expected: 1. The grid navigates to the relevant technician and day.
2. The conflicted shift is brought into view.
notes: Whether it switches view (day/week) or highlights the block is unpinned - observe and record.

title: Red/alarming styling is reserved for conflicts and genuine errors - never used for overtime
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.

2. One technician is booked into OVERTIME on a day WITHOUT any conflict (more hours than their day, sequential non-overlapping shifts within working hours - use the technician's working window carefully, or observe the OT tag day).
3. Capacity Bars are on.
steps: 1. Look at the overtime signals for that day ('OT' tag, amber highlights).
2. Look at a conflicted shift for comparison.
expected: 1. Overtime is signaled with the 'OT' text tag and amber tones - NOT red or alarming styling.
2. Red/alarming styling appears only for conflicts and genuine errors.
notes: Note: overtime that spills past working-day end would itself be an After-hours conflict - the pure-OT setup needs hours summed within the working window via overlapping-free stacking; capture the achievable state live.

title: Day-column headers show a capacity bar - blue fill = aggregate booked vs total available, clamped at 100%, equal track widths
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Capacity Bars are ON in View Options (default).
3. Technicians' working hours are known; shifts exist on at least two days with different total booked hours.
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Look at each day column's header bar.
2. Compare a lightly-booked day with a heavily-booked day.
3. Compare the bars' track widths across days.
expected: 1. Each day header shows a capacity bar; the blue fill represents total technician-hours booked divided by total available (sum of all techs' working hours).
2. A more heavily booked day shows a longer blue fill; the fill never exceeds the track (clamped at 100%).
3. The track width is identical across all days (capacity is not rescaled per day), so bars are comparable at a glance.
notes: Exact bar visuals unpinned (no designs) - confirm live.

title: When aggregate hours exceed capacity, an amber spill extends past the track's right edge with a tick at the 100% line
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars are ON.
3. One day is booked BEYOND the team's total available hours (seed extra shifts).
steps: 1. Look at that day's capacity bar.
expected: 1. An amber segment extends past the right edge of the track, showing the excess.
2. A tick marks the 100% line where the track ends.

title: The 'OT' text tag appears whenever any single technician exceeds their own daily hours - even when the day's aggregate is under capacity
permissions_required: Schedule: Edit to set up; View to observe (spec §14.1).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser with Schedule: Edit.
2. Capacity Bars are ON.
3. On one day, a single technician is booked beyond THEIR daily hours while the team's aggregate for that day remains UNDER total capacity (other techs lightly booked).
steps: 1. Look at that day's capacity bar and header.
expected: 1. An 'OT' tag appears for the day even though the aggregate bar is under 100%.
2. The tag is text, not a color-only signal.
3. Overtime (per-technician) and capacity (aggregate) are independent signals.
notes: 'OT' is the spec's tag text - confirm the exact on-screen tag live.

title: Hovering a capacity bar shows a per-technician breakdown, with overtime technicians highlighted in amber
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. Capacity Bars are ON; a day exists where one technician is in overtime and others are not.
3. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Hover over that day's capacity bar.
2. Read the tooltip.
expected: 1. A tooltip shows a per-technician breakdown: assigned hours vs that technician's capacity.
2. The overtime technician's entry is highlighted in amber.
3. The numbers agree with the shifts actually on the grid.

title: Shift hover tooltip shows customer, unit/vehicle/VIN, date and time, technician, scope, up to 3 line names, and a progress bar
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-line shift exists covering 5 lines, with some time logged.
3. The VIN toggle in 'Filter and Display' is ON (the tooltip shows the VIN only when this toggle is on).
4. You are on the Schedule page in week view.
steps: 1. Hover over the shift block and wait briefly for the tooltip.
2. Read the tooltip from top to bottom.
expected: 1. The tooltip shows: the customer name; unit, vehicle, and VIN; the date and time range; the technician; and a scope summary ('N lines · Xh' style).
2. The individual line names appear as a short list capped at 3, with a '+N more lines' row for the rest (here '+2 more lines'); line statuses are NOT shown.
3. A time-logged progress bar shows logged vs estimated hours ('X / Yh' style).
notes: The 'N lines · Xh', '+N more lines', and 'X / Yh' formats are the spec's wording - confirm the exact copy live. Spec inconsistency (flagged): §4.13 lists the VIN in the tooltip unconditionally, while §9 ties tooltip VIN to the VIN toggle (default OFF) - authored with the toggle ON so the assertion holds either way; the VIN-off tooltip behavior is asserted by SCH-VIEW-04. Verify both toggle states live.

title: A conflicted shift's tooltip shows the conflict icon and the conflict reason in amber
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A conflicted shift exists (for example double-booked).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Hover the conflicted shift and read the tooltip.
expected: 1. The customer name line includes the conflict icon.
2. The conflict reason is shown in amber.

title: Event hover tooltip shows the event name with its grey category dot, date and time range, and technician
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. An event exists on a technician's day.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Hover the event card and read the tooltip.
expected: 1. The tooltip shows the event name with its category dot (grey for a default event).
2. The date and time range are shown.
3. The technician is shown.

title: Tooltips open after a short hover delay, dismiss on mouse-leave, and are read-only - clicking still opens the modal
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A shift exists on the grid.
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Move the mouse quickly across the block without stopping - watch for tooltips.
2. Rest the pointer on the block and wait briefly.
3. Move the mouse off the block.
4. Click the block.
expected: 1. A quick pass does not flash tooltips - the tooltip opens only after a short hover delay (spec: roughly 300 to 500ms).
2. It dismisses when the mouse leaves the block.
3. The tooltip is read-only (no buttons/actions inside it).
4. Clicking the block opens the full detail modal as normal.
notes: The 300-500ms delay is spec-approximate - confirm the actual delay behavior live.

title: The tooltip flips above the block or shifts horizontally to stay within the viewport - it is never clipped
preconditions: 1. You are signed in on a desktop browser.
2. A multi-line shift (tall tooltip) exists near the BOTTOM edge of the viewport, and another near a horizontal edge (scroll to arrange).
3. You are on the Schedule page.
steps: 1. Hover the shift near the bottom edge and look at where its tooltip opens.
2. Hover the shift near the side edge.
expected: 1. When there is not enough room below, the tooltip opens ABOVE the block instead.
2. Near a side edge, the tooltip shifts horizontally to stay fully within the viewport.
3. No part of the tooltip is clipped off-screen.
